segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Valsa Williams with the Midday News.
The headlines.
India and Liechtenstein explore ways to strengthen cooperation in trade, investment,
science, technology and innovation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi holds talks
with hereditary Prince Aloys in New Delhi.
Cyclone Ornab advances towards Andhra Pradesh coast with landfall expected tomorrow.
Odisha braces for extremely heavy rainfall and strong winds in several
southern districts. 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concludes with
adoption of joint declaration, member nations reaffirm commitment to
strengthening parliamentary cooperation and advancing shared goals of
resilience, polling underway in Israel to elect new parliament and in men's
cricket third T20 international between India and New Zealand underway in
Wellington. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held a bilateral meeting with Acting Head of
State of the Principality of Liechtenstein, Heritage Reprints Alloys, at Hyderabad House
in New Delhi. Both leaders discussed on cooperation in various areas including trade and investment,
science, technology and innovation and people-to-people exchanges. They also exchanged views
on regional and global developments. Prince Alloys was accorded ceremonial reception at the
Court of Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning, President Robert E. Murmur and Prime Minister
Narendra Modi welcomed him.
In a media statement, Prince Aloha said, the visit bears testimony to the importance that
Liechtenstein attaches to the relationship with India.
This historic visit bears testimony to the importance that Liechtenstein attaches to
the relationship with India.
The conclusion of the trade and economic partnership agreement, TEPA, with India,
which entered into force a year ago, marked a significant milestone in this regard.
We are determined to build on this momentum and strengthen our ties with India even further.
External Affairs Minister Dr. Jai Shankar called on Prince Alois in a social media post,
Dr. Jai Shankar said the bilateral partnership between India and Liechtenstein
is witnessing strong momentum across a wide range of sectors
as driven by opportunities arising from the India-EFTA trade and economic partnership agreement.
Later, he will also meet President Ropati Murmur at Rasupati Bhavan this evening, who
will also host an official banquet in the honour of the visiting dignitary.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation
Conclave in 2026 at Bharat Mandapur, New Delhi today. He will also address the
gathering on the occasion, a report.
The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas including artificial intelligence, biotechnology,
advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions
will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances
into practical applications. The conclave will also feature an extensive technology
an innovation exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies.
It will include around 150 deep-tech start-up stalls which will highlight technological developments
and their potential applications across sectors.
Anpamesh, Aakashwani News, Delhi.
Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Hardeep Singpuri, has highlighted the resilience
of India's energy management system amid global geopolitical conflicts and disruptions
at key maritime choke points. He was speaking at the inauguration of the 29th Energy Technology
Meet in Goa. The minister said, global crude oil production continues to exceed demand.
Mr. Puri said India has diversified its crude oil supply sources, increasing the number of
supplier countries from 27 to 41.
Union environment, forest and climate change Minister Bhupendra Yadav arrived in Armenia
near Zairevan today to attend the high-level segment of the 17th meeting of the Conference
of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity. In a social media post, the minister
said he would present India's views, efforts and achievements in conserving its rich natural
biodiversity across different bilateral and multilateral forums.
Couting of votes is underway for 11 MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh, 8 in Bihar, 5 in
Maharashtra and four in Karnataka. The voting took place on October 23 for the
biennial elections to the Legislative Council from graduate and teachers
constituencies in these four states. This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR news. Follow us on X at AIR newsalerts and visit newsaunair.gov.in for the
latest updates.
Severe cyclonic storm Ornab is advancing towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and is likely to
make landfall tomorrow morning. The storm is expected to bring extremely heavy rainfall
and strong winds to several southern districts of Odisha. The state government has intensified
disaster preparedness with rescue teams and cyclone shelters kept ready.
Malkankeri, Korapur, Rai, Gajapati and Ganja are among the districts facing the greatest
weather threat.
More in this report.

moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.
The IMD says the system is likely to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam near Yanam
by tomorrow morning, with winds of 115 to 125 km per hour gusting to 140.

It's a raid warning for extremely heavy rainfall forecast tomorrow.
Malkangiri, Kuraput, Raya Gada, Ghazapati and Ganjam are among the most vulnerable districts.
The state government has mobilized disaster response teams, prepared shelters, and restricted
access to vulnerable tourist spots.
Authorities have initiated evacuation of about 48,000 people to safer locations.
Schools in affected districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow.

Prakash Das for Akash Fani News, Bhuvaneswar.
The cyclonic storm continues to rage over the west-central bay of Bengal, moving at a speed
of 20 km per hour over the past six hours, more from our correspondent.
The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continues to rage over the west-central bay of Bengal,
moving at a speed of 20 km per hour over the past six hours.
According to the latest updates, the system is currently centered approximately 220 km
kilometers from Vishakhapatnam, 240 kilometers from Kakinada, 340 kilometers from Majlipatnam
and 410 kilometers from Bapatla.
The Indian Meteorological Department IMD forecatched that cyclone is projected to cross
the coast tomorrow morning between Bapatla and Vishakhapatnam, close to Anam, bringing
gale force winds custing between 125 kilometers and 135 kilometers per hour during landfall.
Under the immediate influence of the cyclone, extensive and widespread rainfall is
already pounding several districts, including Vishakhpatnam, Srikakulam, Vijayanagara, Parvthipuramanyam,
Konisima and Ankapalli. To handle any emergencies, teams from the NDRF and SDRF have been swiftly
deployed across 11 honourable districts. Sathya Narayana, Aakashwani News.
The 12th BRICS parliamentary forum concluded today with the adoption of the joint declaration
unanimously. During the second and final day of the two-day forum, Lok Sabha speaker and
Chairperson of the 12th RIGS Parliamentary Forum, Om Birla, proposed the unanimous adoption
of the joint declaration.
After two days of deliberations, we have arrived at a common consensus.
This joint declaration reflects our commitment to further strengthening parliamentary cooperation
and advancing our shared objectives under the four key themes discussed at the conference
– resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability.
Mr. Birla then handed over the chairship of the BRICS forum for 2027 to China.
Later, Mr. Birla delivered his valedictory address at Central Hall of Samvidhan, southern
in which he called for greater dialogue, trust and cooperation among nations to address
global challenges.
Mr. Birla said despite differences in opinions, backgrounds and challenges, BRICS countries
countries share a common commitment to human welfare, peace and prosperity.
The International Kullu Deshehra, a symbol of Himachal Pradesh's rich folk culture and
unique Dev traditions, will conclude today with the traditional ritual of Lankadahan
in Kullu district. The 7-day festival will come to an end in the presence of Chief Minister
Sukvinder Singh Sokho, who will be the Chief Guest at the closing ceremony or
report.
According to Dev traditions, Lord Raghunath Ji will be taken from his temporary camp
in a chariot this afternoon for the Lanka-the-Hindrachal.
Thereafter, Lord Ragnathji will be carried in a palanquin back to his temple at Sultanpur.
As per age-old traditions and religious customs, the completion of the chariot procession marks
the formal conclusion of Kullu-the-Sherah, following which the deities who arrived from
different parts of the district return to their respective temples.
The final cultural evening of the International Kullu-the-Sherah Festival today will be
dedicated to Himachali folk artists.
With Ritesh Kapoor's report from Shimla, this is Jigasa Pandey, Akashwani News.
news. The historic Rajipadha Rajgeya Murma Jatrafair is said to begin today at Mandar
in Ranchi district of Jharkhand. The two-day state level fair will be formally inaugurated
this evening, more from our Ranchi correspondent. The Rajipadha Rajgeya Murma Jatrafair, a
symbol of Jharkhand's rich tribal culture, deep-rooted faith, and historical heritage
begins today at Mandar in Ranchi. The fair is not merely a cultural gathering
but also a reminder of a centuries-old agreement between the Munda and Orau tribes symbolizing social harmony and unity.
According to local tradition, the agreement was reached when the Orau community migrated from Rohotasgarh to this region with the aim of preserving mutual brotherhood.
The fair continues to commemorate this historical association.
One of its major attractions is the traditional gathering of Sarna flags representing 40 parhas,
where traditional priests and religious leaders from different areas participate along with
their respective courhas or traditional dance groups. Religious rituals will be performed
at the Shakti Khuta located at the Jatra site under the leadership of Sarna religious leader
Bandhantigga. The fair will be formally inaugurated at 5 pm with the lighting of 40 traditional
lamps representing the 40 parhas. Mahavish Rahman, Aakashwani news, Rachi.
Aakashwani will organize the 67th edition of Sardar Vallabhaya Patel lecture series today.
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Shivraj Singh Chauhan will deliver
the lecture.
The recording of the lecture will be broadcast on Sardar Patel's Janthi on the 31st of this
month on the entire Aakashwani network at 9.30pm.
The Supreme Court today sought a response from leaders of the opposition in the Lok
Subhayan Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and others, on a plea which alleged that the Congress leader
pushed a pregnant journalist during a march to the apex court on the 12th of this month.
Marking a hundred years of sporting ties between India and New Zealand,
the Rugby 7 series begins today in Rajgir Bihar. We have more from our correspondent.
Rajgir is all set to witness a blend of sporting enthusiasm and the spirit of friendship
today. The occasion is the rugby seventh series between India and New Zealand, where young players
are ready to thrill spectators with their speed, strength and impressive teamwork.
The matches will begin at 4.20pm with a contest between the men's team,
followed by a match between the women's teams. A special highlight of the series will be
friendly matches featuring mixed men's and women's teams from both countries.
Savita Parikh, Aakashwani news, Patnau.
